newsitem.title: GERMANY: FORECAST-WestLB ups EPS on big German chemicals.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-WestLB ups EPS on big German chemicals.

text.p: Analysts at Germany's WestLB bank said on Wednesday they had again upped their profit outlooks for the three main German chemical companies, forecasting higher margins for the second quarter.
WestLB said that tax reform and exchange rates would support the growth in profits at BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG, while dividend growth had also been better than expected.
BASF remained the favoured stock, but all three were given "outperformer" status by the Duesseldorf bank.
WestLB lifted its earnings per share (EPS) forecast at BASF for 1997 to 4.90 marks from 4.65 marks and to 4.75 marks from 4.35 marks for 1998.
EPS for Bayer was upped to 3.95 marks from 3.90 marks in 1997 and to 4.10 marks from 3.95 marks in 1998.
The bank upped its forecast for Hoechst to 4.10 marks from 4.05 marks and to 4.35 marks from 4.25 marks for 1998.
This is the second time WestLB has upped its EPS outlooks for the leading chemical stocks in six weeks.
Shares in the three blue-chip companies were among the most sought-after shares in afternoon electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index on Wednesday.

BASF was up 17 pfennigs at 63.35 marks, Bayer was up 53 pfennigs at 67.45 marks and Hoechst was up 43 pfennigs at 75.38 marks. All three were off earlier highs as the market came off its record levels earlier on.
